html:
SMTO-GWT-0056 — File transfer did not complete

GUID: a6671669-f806-4d1a-a243-b5823520205e
Slug: transfer-failed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO was copying a file from one Gateway computer to another, and the copy stopped before it finished. The file at the destination was not replaced.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation why the copy stopped; it can read the reason from the failed copy step. The reason, such as the file changing during the copy or being too large, decides what to fix.
  2. Fix that cause: wait until the source file is no longer being changed, or free space or pick a different folder on the destination computer. Copying again without fixing the cause will stop in the same place.
  3. Check the destination folder to confirm the file there is still the old version or absent, then ask SMTO to copy it again. This copy didn't replace the destination, so a fresh copy is safe once the cause is fixed.

What success looks like

  • A new copy finishes and SMTO reports that the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the two Gateway computers. Don't copy the file over the destination some other way until you've checked what is there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • gateway.copy failed before a verified destination commit; the transfer checkpoint was marked aborted, the destination is reported unchanged, and the result records the error_kind and any incomplete staging cleanup.

What this means

  • Transfer orchestration caught a failure without a verified destination publication; its retained commit phase and effect flags determine whether the destination is known unchanged. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Transfer orchestration caught a failure without a verified destination publication; its retained commit phase and effect flags determine whether the destination is known unchanged.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the transfer ID, last checkpoint, bytes acknowledged, commit state and cleanup receipt before resuming any work.

How to fix it

  • Read the copy result's error_kind (for example revision_conflict, quota_exceeded or invalid_transfer_chunk) and its cleanup fields, plus the source and destination Gateway logs, to find the cause. Fix that cause, confirm the destination path's current state and that staging cleanup completed, then start a new gateway.copy.
  • Inspect the original checkpoint, destination and cleanup evidence. Use supported recovery only for work still required under its owning task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The original transfer's destination and cleanup state are reconciled before a supported continuation or replacement.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
